## setting
**100 run(s)** — rule `pt25-setting` — 10.1186/s12864-025-12230-4  
*Methods, 'RNAseq and differential expression analyses'; Results*

> A total of 100 Pt-infected wheat FIELD SAMPLES were subjected to RNA extraction using the RNeasy Plant Mini Kit. | Pt76_024702 was highly expressed in FIELD-COLLECTED Pt-infected plant samples collected ACROSS 11 COUNTRIES (100 RNA-seq datasets analysed). | The controlled work in the same paper is separate and is for GENOMES, not these libraries: 'harvested from 66 Pt isolates and multiplied by successive rounds of inoculation on the susceptible wheat varieties Armada or Michigan Amber. For each round of inoculation, wheat plants were grown in controlled conditions (16-h light/8-h dark and 18 degC/12 degC cycles)' - the deposit carries 71 WGS runs alongside the 100 RNA-Seq ones.

## location
**100 run(s)** — rule `tsu25-PRJEB84390-location` — 10.1186/s12864-025-12230-4  
*Additional file 1 (12864_2025_12230_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx), sheet "Table S13"*

> Per-isolate table, 100 rows, one per RNA-seq dataset: Isolate name, Collection year, Country, Location, Host variety, Accession, Alignment rate. The body text ties it to the deposit: '100 RNA-seq datasets derived from field-collected Pt-infected plant samples across 11 countries'. Location is a county or town for 40 rows and the literal '-' for the other 60, so the supplement itself states that no finer site was recorded for those. ENA's own `location` column is EMPTY for all 171 runs in PRJEB84390, which is why these 100 sat on country centroids. Keyed by Accession, an ENA secondary sample accession (ERS); tsu25.py resolves ERS to run through the cached ENA portal table. The Polish place names are corrupted in the supplied xlsx (Jaroseawiec for Jaroslawiec, Guvcz for Gurcz, both already in the cohort under the correct spelling from PRJEB15280 and PRJEB39201); they are emitted as written and repaired in missing_localities.tsv.
